name: Osskar Mango-Habanero Fire Rocks
description: Popping hard candy pieces in mango-orange with a habanero oil core — when the candy dissolves to the center, it releases both the heat and a small carbonation burst. Sold in tiny foil envelopes, often from vending machines.
flavor_profile: Sweet, slightly artificial mango upfront; as the shell dissolves, a genuine habanero bloom and carbonation pop arrive simultaneously, creating a heat-and-fizz sensation that fades in about 30 seconds
slogan: The pop you didn't see coming.
cultural_context: Osskar Fire Rocks are a rite of passage on the Shelf — daring someone to hold three in their mouth at once is a playground game with a long history. Adults buy them nostalgically. The tiny foil envelopes are collectible; Osskar prints rotating street-art imagery on them.
story_hooks: Osskar's founder died years ago and left the brand to a collective of Shelf residents who now run it communally — a larger confectioner is attempting a hostile acquisition by quietly buying out individual collective members one by one.

A limited-edition Fire Rocks envelope design features a piece of art that turns out to contain a hidden encoded message — whether it was intentional or a strange coincidence is unclear, but people are now obsessively buying every envelope to find the rest of the pattern.
A character uses the popping sensation of Fire Rocks to mask the sound and sensation of a subdermal implant activating — a small, strange, very Shelf-district piece of tradecraft.
